prerequisites: Has knowledge of basic mechanical properties of engineering materials.
Have a basic knowledge of physics and mathematics.
Have skills in measurement methods, techniques for measuring and evaluating the results of the measurement.

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic technologies and material plastic forming process parameters.
Able to properly define the problem in the field of plastic forming and properly be characterized.
Can choose the right technology plastic forming and defining the basic parameters of the process.
Can search for information on plastic forming and execute their critical analysis.
Can use the theoretical knowledge gained in forming the lecture and apply it in practice.
Able to perform selected laboratory tests and correct to assess their performance.
Can think and act in a creative way.
Acquires the ability to work as a team.

syllabus_topics: History of plastic processing.
Effect of strain on the structure and properties of the material.
Effect of plastic forming process on the properties of the product.
Sheet metal forming processes. Analysis of cutting and bending processes.
Course of process of formation of articles about non - the developable surface.
Processes of forming lumps. Analysis of the process of rolling plates and profiles.
The conduct and analysis of the extrusion process.
The course and forging process analysis.
Manufacture of metal in the drawing process.
Manufacture of metal in the metal powder metallurgy.
Metal Forming Tools.
Overview of modern technologies for shaping plastic.
Final test
Cold deformation and annealing of metals.
Cupping test sheets.
Rolled metal sheets and profiles.
Squeezing metallurgical and machine parts.
Manufacture of metal in the process of drawing.
Expression - cut, bending and pressing.
Free forging and matrix.
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
self study - preparation for laboratory class

assessment_methods.method: quizzes, laboratory report, participate in discussions problem (Laboratory)

assessment_rules: Lecture evaluation is based on a colloquium (F1). The final grade (P) for the lecture is equal to F1. Laboratory evaluation involves quizzes, laboratory reports, and participation in problem discussions (F1). The final grade (P) for the laboratory is equal to F1.
